subject: Hosted API volume slabs, commit tiers, and model-differential (embeddings vs chat)
messages:
From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@skybound.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@skybound.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API — clarifying volume slabs / model premiums

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers on the chat endpoint looked great. Procurement asked me to get a few specifics before we move to a formal SOW:

- How do your per-token tiers stack for hosted usage? We expect a mix of chat traffic (user prompts + assistant) and a steady stream of embeddings for search indexing.
- Are embeddings priced separately from chat generation? If so, how do the slabs apply when both hit the same monthly commit?
- We also want clarity on "premium" models vs standard: what multiplier or surcharge should we expect for certain model families (e.g., RLHF-tuned or larger capacity variants)?

Can you send a simple table and a recommended commit/discount plan for our expected profile (approx 2B tokens chat + 1B tokens embeddings / month to start)?

Also, procurement prefers to see any documents as attachments rather than inline links.

Appreciate it —
Sarah
Sarah Miller
Director of Platform Engineering
Skybound Analytics

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@skybound.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — clarifying volume slabs / model premiums

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short summary and attached two files: a one-page pricing summary and an XLSX that breaks down per-token math by slab and model family. High-level answers below, then Monica will follow with the concrete numbers for the 2B/1B profile.

- Per-token tiers: our hosted API offers slabbed unit pricing with four committed bands (0-250M, 250M-1B, 1B-5B, 5B+). Each slab has a baseline per-token for standard chat models. Committed discounts apply to the entire monthly usage after you hit the slab threshold.
- Embeddings vs chat: embeddings are billed separately (different per-token unit) and do not auto-offset chat tokens. However, when you sign a blended commit (single monthly dollar commitment), we can offer cross-product slabing that effectively blends the two if you provide an expected usage mix.
- Premium models: certain model families (e.g., prod-advanced-xxl, rlhf-plus) have a multiplicative premium applied on top of the slab baseline. The premium is model-specific and shown as a multiplier in the sheet. For modest volume we usually recommend a mixed-pin approach: pin mission-critical traffic to a premium model but route lower-priority or heavy-embedding traffic to a standard/quantized variant.

Monica — can you attach the slab numbers and a recommended commit tier for 2B chat / 1B embeddings? Also include an example blended commit option (monthly $ commit + blended token discount) and a strict per-token only commit so Skybound can compare.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@skybound.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — clarifying volume slabs / model premiums

Hi Sarah & Naomi,

Attached the two files you requested: SB-SOW-v1.pdf (draft SOW with term and deliverables) and redwood-pricing-models-compare.xlsx. Key excerpts from the spreadsheet below for quick scanning:

- Baseline per-token (standard chat): $0.0000020 per token in 1B-5B slab
- Baseline embeddings (standard): $0.0000010 per token in 1B-5B slab
- Premium model multiplier: 1.6x for prod-advanced-xxl, 1.25x for rlhf-plus-small; we show both absolute and blended pricing tabs.
- Blended commit example (recommended): $60k/month commit for 3B combined tokens (2B chat, 1B embeddings) -> effective blended price: chat $0.0000016, embeddings $0.0000008 (reflects 12% additional discount vs pure per-token)
- Strict per-token commit example: commit to 2B chat only at $48k/month -> chat effective $0.0000019; embeddings billed at standard on-demand rates unless you add a small embeddings reserve.

Notes and tradeoffs: if you expect sustained growth >5B tokens in future quarters, moving to a 5B+ slab with a higher monthly commit increases savings substantially. Also consider pinning 20% of production traffic to a premium family and routing the rest to a standard family; the spreadsheet simulates that mixed split.

Attachments: SB-SOW-v1.pdf (draft legal/term language), redwood-pricing-models-compare.xlsx (detailed math, slider tabs).

Let us know which commit example you want us to build into contract language and I can push a DocuSign SOW.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@skybound.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — clarifying volume slabs / model premiums

Naomi / Monica —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — the spreadsheet is very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and engineering:

1) Procurement prefers the blended commit model but wants a floor clause: if actual combined usage is below 85% of the commit for two consecutive months, they request either an invoice credit mechanism or the ability to step down a slab once. Is Redwood open to a 90-day lookback with a 2-step downgrade (with defined crediting) written into the SOW?

2) Engineering question: for embeddings vs chat, will the KV cache / prefix caching behavior affect billing if we re-use generated tokens as part of embedding pre-processing (e.g., we send the same prompt to both chat and embeddings pipelines)? In short, is there any double-billing risk for identical token payloads hitting different endpoints?

3) Premium-pin: we like the idea of pinning a % to premium. Can you give an example where 20% pinned produces x% delta in the effective blended rate vs 0% pin? The spreadsheet shows it but procurement wants a one-paragraph explanation we can paste into their internal approval.

If you can answer (1)-(3) and then convert the preferred blended example into a DocuSign SOW, procurement will aim to approve by EOD Friday.

Best,
Sarah

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@skybound.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — clarifying volume slabs / model premiums

Sarah —

Short answers to keep procurement moving, with Rishi copied for the formal SOW language and billing/legal nuances:

1) Floor / downgrade: yes — we can do a 90-day lookback with a 2-step downgrade and a pro-rata credit applied to shortfall months. We will surface the exact step amounts in the SOW (Monica/Rishi to draft). This will be linked in the SOW attachments (we included a placeholder clause in SB-SOW-v1.pdf).

2) Double-billing risk for identical token payloads: billed per API endpoint invocation. If you send the same prompt payload to both the chat and embeddings endpoints, each request will be billed on the respective unit (chat tokens vs embedding tokens). However, if you use our prefix/KV caching for chat generation and you re-use the same cached KV across requests, that can reduce tokens sent downstream; caching savings are applied on a per-route basis. If you architect a pipeline that fans out a single sanitized payload to both endpoints, treat them as separate billable requests — meaning engineering should prefer producing embeddings from the minimal tokenized text (avoid sending assistant replies into the embedding call).

3) Pin example (one paragraph): Pinning 20% of production to a premium model increases the weighted cost by the premium multiplier on that 20% while letting 80% remain at baseline. For example, with a 1.6x premium on 20% of 2B chat tokens, the weighted chat cost increases by 0.6 * 0.2 = 12% on the chat portion; when blended with the embeddings discount in the recommended commit, the net effective spend increase is about 8% overall vs a 0% pin scenario while preserving higher-quality responses on critical traffic.

Next steps: Monica will send a version of the SOW with the floor clause spelled out and a DocuSign-ready package. I'll also include the short paragraph above in the SOW appendix so procurement can paste it.

Thanks — aiming for the DocuSign today.
Naomi Feldman
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
